sample_unit: AOSLO images (three datasets: low-quality out-of-domain, high-quality out-of-domain, in-domain)

links.outcome: Cone detector Dice on out-of-domain low-quality AOSLO images versus in-domain images
links.effect: Out-of-domain LQ mean Dice was 0.47 (recall 0.37) without NST versus 0.88 on the in-domain dataset; NST raised LQ Dice to 0.84 (recall 0.92, precision 0.83).
links.quote: Our NST approach substantially improved mean Dice on the LQ dataset from 0.47 to 0.84, primarily by increasing recall (from 0.37 to 0.92) with a limited reduction in precision (from 0.95 to 0.83).

unlisted_practices: Test-time neural style transfer to harmonize image appearance between training and target domains without retraining
Comparing test-time augmentation methods (WCT, photorealistic patch transfer, histogram matching/equalization, AdaIN) for domain adaptation

screen.reason: The study empirically tests a model-agnostic test-time augmentation safeguard (neural style transfer domain harmonization) added to an existing deep learning diagnostic model to mitigate domain shift across datasets.
